Mumbai · H/W Ward

open spaces on the plan. Most of them small.

H/W Ward, Bandra West: one of Mumbai's 24 wards, between the sea and the Western Railway, home to an estimated people. Its Development Plan marks open spaces, shown in green; of them exist today.

NAGAR & UDRI's ward-by-ward map (2025, on 2011–18 data) puts H/W at 2.8 m² of open space per person, 1.5 existing and 1.3 reserved; this atlas, on the 2026 population, gives 1.36 and 1.14.

Open space per person in H/W

It's nearly the size of a yoga mat.

The open space that exists in H/W today works out to m² per resident, barely more than a 1.1 m² yoga mat. WHO's 9 m² minimum is a room 3 m by 3 m.

What exists, what is promised

exist only on paper.

acres of open space exist in H/W today. Another acres are reserved on the Development Plan: land set aside, not yet a park, playground or garden.

The clock on reserved land

From 2028, it can be lost.

DP 2034 came into force in 2018. Once a reservation is ten years old and still not acquired, its owner can serve MCGM a purchase notice; if MCGM takes no steps within 24 months, the land is released from the reservation. Every one of H/W's reservations is on that clock unless MCGM has already bought it.

Satellite estimate of what is on the reserved land today: Google Open Buildings 2.5D (2023) and Esri imagery (Nov 2025); to be confirmed on site. Lifecycle after NAGAR & UDRI, Public Open Space Mapping and Management Strategy for Mumbai (2025). MRTP Act 1966, s.127 (24-month window since 2015).

Sources and notes

Population: about 3,25,000 in 2026. This is BMC's own ward projection (3,24,016 for 2025, as compiled by Praja's ward-wise budget report, 2025), extended one year at the same rate of ~1,150 people a year. The last census count was 3,07,581 (2011, MCGM census FAQ), Praja reports that 39% of residents live in slums; MCGM's census page gives a lower 27% (82,552 people in 2011). The two have not been reconciled, and the atlas leads with Praja's figure. India's next count, Census 2027, enumerates in February 2027. Ward area is from MCGM's DP 2034 ward-boundary GIS (8.7 km²), which stops at the old shoreline; eighteen sea-face reservations tagged H/W (about 44 acres) lie seaward of it and are included. Benchmarks: Mumbai's existing public open space of 1.28 m² per person and the DP 2034 target of 3.37 m² per person are figures MCGM published with the DP in 2018. 10–12 m² per person is the URDPFI guideline (MoHUA, 2014). 9 m² is the WHO figure widely cited in Indian planning literature. "Existing" means designated as existing (EOS) in DP 2034, not verified on site. Reservations (ROS) are land set aside for open space, much of it not yet acquired or developed.

Data, method and limitations

Source

Geometry and attributes come from MCGM's own Development Plan 2034 GIS, the map service behind the DP Remarks portal (dpremarks.mcgm.gov.in). It was queried on for every feature intersecting the H/W Ward boundary, plus sea-face reservations tagged H/W that lie seaward of it (see Limitations).

What is counted

  • EOS: existing open-space designations (PLU designation layer), e.g. EOS1.4 Playground, EOS1.5 Garden/Park, EOS2.6 Recreation Ground.
  • ROS: open-space reservations (PLU reservation layer), e.g. ROS1.4, ROS1.5, ROS2.3, ROS2.4.
  • Composite codes containing an open-space component (e.g. EE1.2+EOS1.4, ROS1.5+RT1.6) are included under their open-space category and flagged.
  • Layout RG: recreation grounds required in private layouts and shown on the DP.
  • Water bodies: one tank is designated EOS1.1. Two further ponds from the DP water-bodies layer are shown so they can be studied, but they carry no EOS/ROS code. Nallas and the river are context only.
  • Natural areas, NDZ, mangroves and forest zones are excluded by design.

Method

  • A plot is in scope if at least half its area lies inside MCGM's H/W ward boundary.
  • Areas are computed in WGS 84 / UTM 43N (EPSG:32643). They agree with MCGM's recorded SHAPE.AREA to within 0.02% for every plot.
  • CTS numbers come from overlaying each plot on MCGM's property (CTS/CS) layer. A parcel is listed if it overlaps the plot by at least 25 m² and makes up at least 5% of the plot or 20% of the parcel.
  • Village is the DP village boundary containing most of the plot. All H/W villages fall in Mumbai Suburban District.
  • DP reference IDs (e.g. H/WR082), sheet numbers and names come from the DP label points that fall inside each plot.

Limitations

  • Names are rarely recorded in the DP data. Most plots are identified by code, CTS number and village only.
  • Plots are DP polygons, not sites. One reservation split by a road appears as several plots that share a DP reference.
  • DP designation shows land-use intent, not condition, access or ownership. "Existing" means designated as existing in DP 2034, not verified on site.
  • MCGM's ward polygons stop at the old shoreline. Eighteen sea-face reservations (about 44 acres, along Bandstand, Bandra Reclamation, Carter Road and Khar Danda, several on the sea side of the Coastal Road) are tagged H/W but fall in no ward polygon. They are included here, have no village or CTS number, and are listed in the QA report.
  • The portal is updated with modifications over time. Re-run the scripts to refresh.
